title: Chiral oxazolidinones via biocatalytic aziridination of unactivated alkenes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the 42.8 MB Supplementary Information Word file (41586_2026_11169_MOESM1_ESM.docx): 434 zip entries, 401 embedded images, 57 Word tables, 129,934 characters of text. Counted the tables and their rows by hand-parsing the XML: 28 'calibration curve and data analysis' blocks (products 3a-3z, 4, 7), each a 4-row table of duplicate yield measurements; Table S11/S12 list 9 + 4 evolved enzyme variants and their mutations; Table S9 lists 11 initial-screen wells; Table S10 lists 4 protecting groups; Table S17 holds 33 rows of quantum-chemistry energies. Found 13 DNA sequences (591 nucleotides each) and 13 protein sequences (197 amino acids each). Found zero SMILES strings (machine-readable chemical structure text) and zero InChI identifiers. Also read the Zenodo deposit metadata and README (4 files, 13.3 MB: AMBER molecular-dynamics topologies, coordinates, input scripts and PDB snapshots for 7 simulated systems, CC-BY-4.0). Also downloaded and read the 3.2 MB peer review file.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The Nature article itself is paywalled (Europe PMC: not open access, no PMC identifier) and its Data availability statement is not visible in the public HTML, so I could not read it. Main-text figure panels (the substrate scope with enantiomeric excess values, and the evolution trajectory chart) are images I could not parse; the enantiomeric excess numbers for most scope entries live in those figures and in chiral HPLC chromatogram images, not in any table I could extract. The claim that ~400 recombination variants were sequenced comes from the authors' rebuttal letter; that table was not extractable as text and is not deposited anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplementary Word file and the Zenodo molecular-dynamics deposit (CC-BY-4.0) both downloaded without login. But the Zenodo deposit is simulation input files for 7 systems, not a measurement table; all measured numbers live inside the Word document.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Yield (%) is a genuine column in 28 small Word tables. Enantiomeric excess (ee, the purity of one mirror-image form) is mostly in figure images, so the ee label would have to be read off pictures - borderline, but yield alone passes.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked the files: zero SMILES and zero InChI strings (both are text formats for chemical structures). Every substrate is a drawn chemical structure in one of 401 embedded images, labelled only '1a', '1b'. Each input would have to be hand-drawn into a structure by a chemist.

a4_units_stated.note: Verified in the tables: 'Yield (%)', 'Conc. (M)', 'ee (%)', 'STDEV' column headers are explicit and consistent across all 28 scope tables.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted in the files: 28 substrate-scope products, 13 evolved enzyme variants, 11 initial-screen wells, 4 protecting groups, each measured in duplicate. Total unique measured reactions is roughly 100-150, far under the 1,500-row (or 400-row classification) threshold.

a6_fits_laptop.note: 42.8 MB Word file plus 13.3 MB Zenodo archive; everything opens in memory on a laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Table counts in the file are internally consistent and match the reviewers' and authors' descriptions in the peer review file (9-round OxazS lineage, 4-round StzS lineage, scope 3a-3z).

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are real bench measurements: HPLC-MS product-to-internal-standard ratios converted through calibration curves, and chiral HPLC for enantiomeric excess. Not model output.

part_a_killers._note: Stopped at the first two failures (A3 and A5); remaining items recorded for completeness since they were already verified in the same pass.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: with roughly 100-150 measured reactions, 28 substrates and 13 enzyme variants, any model would be fitting noise rather than learning sequence-substrate-selectivity rules.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use enzyme sequence and substrate structure to predict how much product a heme enzyme makes and which mirror image it favours.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one enzyme variant paired with one alkene substrate: the 197-amino-acid protoglobin sequence plus the substrate's chemical structure. Verified counts: 13 enzyme sequences and 28 substrate-scope products, so at most ~150 measured reactions.
plain_idea.predict: Yield as a percentage and enantiomeric excess (how strongly one mirror-image product dominates). Truth comes from bench measurements: product-to-internal-standard ratios on HPLC-MS against calibration curves, and chiral HPLC for the mirror-image ratio.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Biocatalysis groups like the Arnold lab at Caltech would use a working sequence-to-selectivity model to skip rounds of directed evolution; here, though, the measurement count is far too small to train or honestly test one.

ml_idea: The project considered was predicting reaction yield and enantiomeric excess from the pair (enzyme variant sequence, substrate structure) for a heme-protein nitrene-transfer aziridination, using a protein language model such as ESM-2 for the enzyme and a molecular model such as ChemBERTa for the substrate. It dies on data volume: the whole paper contains about 100-150 measured reactions, one enzyme scaffold and one reaction type.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed for modelling: parsing the Word file took seconds, but every substrate would need a chemist to convert a drawn structure into a SMILES string by hand (~28 structures, plus checking), and enantiomeric excess values would need reading off figure images - hence ~20 hours for a table of only ~150 rows.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct measured reactions in the supplementary tables. I did: 28 substrate-scope entries plus 13 variants plus 11 screening wells, around 150 total - under one-tenth of the minimum useful size.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A5 and A3, both verified by opening the files. A5: the entire paper yields roughly 100-150 measured reactions (28 substrates, 13 enzyme variants, 11 screening wells), an order of magnitude under the 1,500-row threshold and well under even the 400-row classification floor. A3: no machine-readable chemical structures exist anywhere - zero SMILES and zero InChI strings in 129,934 characters of supplementary text, with every substrate drawn as one of 401 embedded images. The only formal deposit (Zenodo 21496297, CC-BY-4.0) is molecular-dynamics input files for 7 simulated systems, which contain no labels at all. The science is excellent and the enzyme sequences are clean, but this is a synthesis paper, not a dataset. If the ~400-variant recombination library with every-variant sequencing mentioned in the authors' rebuttal were ever deposited as a table, that would be worth a fresh look.
